_doc: Routing-accuracy fixtures for route.py --hook. Each case asserts what the bridge must do with a representative prompt. `expect_id` pins the winning lane, `expect_silent` requires empty output, `max_tier` forbids a full briefing (the expensive path), `forbid_id` names a lane that must never win, and `forbid_reply_rules` guards the Discord tone contract against leaking into engineering turns. `total_char_budget` caps the whole set so a token regression fails CI.
_budget_note: Sized for the current case count with ~10 percent headroom. Raise it only when cases are added, and record the split between new cases and real growth; a budget raised to make a regression pass defeats the check.

cases.prompt: run the security consent audit
cases.why: The prompt names every word of the workflow id; a sibling that merely repeats 'security' must not win.

cases.prompt: the CI is red on main, what happened
cases.why: Kebab-case ids must tokenize so 'CI' can reach the CI lane instead of the far more expensive PR-review briefing.

cases.prompt: update the docs for the MCP surface
cases.why: Owner/spoke MCP lane, not a generic docs lane.

cases.prompt: review this PR for regressions before merging
cases.why: A workflow and skill share this id; the workflow is the actionable unit that composes owner + spoke.

cases.prompt: verify android and ios parity for the location plugin
cases.why: Tri-flow parity work belongs to the mobile lane.

cases.prompt: deploy the frontend to UAT
cases.why: Scoped deploy lane.

cases.prompt: check cache coherence on the consent center route
cases.why: Named spoke concern, not generic frontend work.

cases.prompt: draft a reply for the discord community question about BYOK
cases.why: This is the one lane that genuinely needs the Discord tone contract.

cases.prompt: why is the vault not decrypting PKM entries on iOS?
cases.why: A question mark in an engineering prompt must not pull in 180 lines of community reply rules.

cases.prompt: who owns the analytics event taxonomy?
cases.why: Same guard, on the skill path.

cases.prompt: how does repo-operations manage branch protection and merge queue settings?
cases.why: Same guard, on the exact-name path.

cases.prompt: hey, what's up
cases.why: Chitchat must never cost tokens.

cases.prompt: make the chart colors nicer
cases.why: No lane owns this; silence beats a confident wrong answer.

cases.prompt: refactor this function to be cleaner
cases.why: Generic engineering verbs must not route anywhere.

cases.prompt: audit the documentation structure of the repo
cases.why: 'audit' is a near-universal word; a low-confidence match must stay a pointer, and must not land on the security lane.

cases.prompt: fix the feed page styling on mobile
cases.why: Ambiguous between the frontend and mobile lanes; a pointer is honest, a full playbook is not.

cases.prompt: the top app bar is not visible on the feed route
cases.why: Weak signal; must not spend a full briefing on a guess.

cases.prompt: let's think about the roadmap for next quarter
cases.why: Planning intent is real but imprecise.

cases.prompt: governor
cases.why: Exact agent name bypasses the length floor and the confidence tiers.

cases.prompt: add a new backend route for consent scopes
cases.why: New surface work routes to the tri-flow feature lane.

cases.prompt: should I respond to this review comment on the PR?
cases.why: 'respond to' plus a question mark is a routine PR turn, not a Discord reply.

cases.prompt: attribution author green hussh land github email commit contributions
cases.why: A workflow scoring below its full gate must stay a pointer even when a same-named skill scores higher; the two scores come from different corpora.

cases.prompt: the Kai chat panel does not stream tokens
cases.why: KNOWN GAP, pinned deliberately. This used to reach one-voice-governance and is now silent: the workflow lands exactly on the lower gate, then loses a same-score tie on alphabetical order and is vetoed by an unrelated skill scoring one point higher across a different corpus. Silence is wrong here. This case exists so a calibration change that fixes it FAILS and has to be acknowledged, rather than passing unnoticed.
